title: Training Note — The Months of Point Overage Required Up Front at a Settlement
content:
# Training Note — The Months of Point Overage Required Up Front at a Settlement

**For how many months is the point overage required up front when a plan under the Building Automation Service Plans is settled?** Where the plan's covered points stand above the tier's covered maximum and the tier trues its licence up quarterly or monthly, the point overage is required up front for the three months to the next true-up, that is for 3 whole months. Where the plan's covered points stand above the tier's covered maximum and the tier trues its licence up annually or semiannually, the point overage is required up front for every whole month left in the plan term. In every other case no months at all are required up front.

| Covered points against the tier's covered maximum | Tier's licence true-up | Months required up front |
|---|---|---|
| above it | quarterly or monthly | the 3 months to the next true-up |
| above it | annual or semiannual | every whole month left in the plan term |
| at or below it | any | no months at all |

**What if the covered points stand exactly at the tier's covered maximum?** No months at all: the first two rows need the covered points to stand above the maximum.

**How are the whole months left in the term counted?** From the handling day to the plan's term end date, whole months only.

**Worked figure (hypothetical).** A plan covering 1560 points at a tier whose covered maximum is 1500 points and whose licence is trued up semiannually, with 7 whole months left in the term, carries the point overage for those 7 months: 60 points multiplied by the tier's point overage fee of 6 USD a point a year, that is 360 USD a year, taken for 7 of the twelve months of a year, that is 210.00 USD. Were the same plan trued up quarterly, the 3 months to the next true-up would be taken, that is 90.00 USD.
